reason: Research was limited: three web searches and one fetch, with no Oct 9 closing data found, so this rests on the packet marks plus Oct 5-6 market reports. The trend legs entered 10-05 are four sessions old and every one sits well inside its stop. MTUM is -1.0% against a 12% stop, QUAL +0.6%, XLE +2.6% and GDX +2.1%, with gold near $4,180 and Brent around $100 on Middle East risk. The reports do not break the trends these legs ride: the Nasdaq-100 and Nvidia were near records, and long yields printed 24-year highs (30y at 5.70%) on Oct 5, with a full 25bp Fed hike priced by December. The TLT short at -1.1% reflects the Oct 6 pullback in yields from those highs, but it is still far from its 8% stop and the hike-pricing that drives it is intact. The XLY short at -2.2% against a 10% stop is the leg most exposed to a broad rally, but the weak-consumer thesis behind it, the 29K payroll print, has not been contradicted by anything I found. Replacing a book this young on noise would pay frictions to chase four days of P&L, which is the whipsaw a trend book must avoid; two field-wide stops this week hit legs only three sessions old. The book as registered already satisfied the Round 3 novelty rule versus Round 2 (no shared names). Hold.
